Services Overview: Customer is looking to migrate its existing Hadoop-based Data Lake (San Antonio environment) to Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The primary objective is to enable business units (Finance, Operations, and Analytics) with equal or enhanced capabilities for data-driven decision-making and self-service insights through BigQuery.

The project leverages Onix’s proprietary automated migration toolset to accelerate the transition. This includes automated code conversion for Hadoop-native objects, structured data ingestion pipeline configuration, orchestration via Cloud Composer (Airflow), and rigorous automated data validation using the Pelican framework.
The scope encompasses end-to-end delivery: from technical discovery and future-state architecture design to execution, testing, and a 30-day post-migration warranty support period.

Program Governance and Leadership: Establish a Program Steering Committee (PSC) consisting of Customer stakeholders and Onix leadership to oversee strategic alignment and high-level escalations.
Conduct a formal Project Kick-off Meeting to finalize project charter, communication protocols, and RACI (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) matrix.
Implement a tiered communication plan: Weekly Tactical Status Meetings, Bi-weekly Management Reviews, and Monthly Executive Briefings.
Establish a centralized Project Management Office (PMO) portal for real-time tracking of milestones, deliverables, and resource allocation.
Manage a formalized Risk, Action, Issue, and Decision (RAID) log with proactive mitigation strategies and clear ownership.
Change Management and Control: Define and implement a Change Request (CR) process to manage deviations from the agreed SOW scope, timeline, or budget.
Conduct impact assessments for all proposed changes, ensuring technical and financial implications are documented and approved by the Steering Committee.
Provide organizational change management (OCM) guidance to assist Customer teams in transitioning from Hadoop-native workflows to GCP-native operations.
Program Planning and Execution: Develop a Comprehensive Integrated Project Plan (IPP) including critical path analysis, resource leveling, and inter-dependency mapping.
Define 'Definition of Ready' (DoR) and 'Definition of Done' (DoD) for each migration sprint to ensure quality and consistency.
Monitor program success metrics (KPIs) including migration velocity, code conversion accuracy rates, and budget burn rates.

Discovery and Analysis: Deep-dive assessment of the SA Hadoop ecosystem including HDFS storage patterns, Hive/Impala metadata, and Spark/MapReduce workload profiles.
Map technical requirements to functional business outcomes to ensure data lineage and logic integrity.
Analyze data volumetrics and growth patterns to optimize BigQuery partitioning and clustering strategies.
Identify and document all upstream/downstream dependencies, including third-party data feeds and consumer applications.
Conduct a Complexity Analysis for 200+ ETL pipelines to categorize migration paths (Automated vs. Manual remediation).
Future State Architecture and Design: Design a scalable GCP Technical Architecture incorporating BigQuery (Storage/Compute), Cloud Composer (Orchestration), and Cloud Logging/Monitoring.
Establish a Data Migration Strategy focusing on minimal downtime, utilizing Connexio for high-velocity historical data transfer.
Develop a Security Architecture including Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles, Service Account governance, and VPC-Service Controls (VPC-SC) alignment.
Formulate a Testing and Validation Strategy using Pelican to automate cell-level data parity checks between Hadoop and BigQuery.
Delivery of a Disaster Recovery (DR) and High Availability (HA) blueprint for the migrated workloads.
Data Ingestion and Pipeline Engineering: Configure and optimize Connexio/FTAAS pipelines for up to 200 tables to support incremental and full-load patterns in GCP.
Refactor up to 50 complex ingestion scripts (Bash, Python, Java) into GCP-native equivalents (e.g., Cloud Functions, Dataflow, or Python-based Composer tasks).
Migrate and validate 750+ derived tables within the SA domain, ensuring transformation logic remains consistent with legacy outputs.
Implement robust error-handling, logging, and alerting frameworks within Cloud Composer for all migrated pipelines.
Code Conversion and Optimization: Execute automated conversion of Hadoop DDLs, Views, and stored procedures to BigQuery-standard SQL (GoogleSQL).
Optimize converted SQL queries to leverage BigQuery-specific features such as nested and repeated fields (JSON/Structs) where beneficial.
Perform manual remediation for complex logic (up to 20% of the 200 pipelines) that cannot be fully translated by automated tools.
Security and Compliance Integration: Ensure all data movement and storage adhere to Customer’s enterprise security standards, including Encryption at Rest and in Transit.
Implement Column-Level Security (CLS) and Row-Level Security (RLS) in BigQuery as defined during the design phase.
Align migration activities with regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, or industry-specific audits) relevant to the San Antonio data domain.

Onix Responsibilities: Provision of migration experts, architects, and tool-specialists.
Technical execution of code conversion, pipeline setup, and Pelican testing.
Project management, status reporting, and deliverable quality assurance.
Handover documentation and 30-day post-migration hypercare support.
Customer Responsibilities: Provision of timely access to source Hadoop environments, GCP projects, and required network/VPN connectivity.
Subject Matter Expert (SME) availability for functional logic validation and requirement clarifications.
Final User Acceptance Testing (UAT) execution and sign-off.
Ownership of third-party software licensing (excluding Onix tools) and GCP consumption costs.

General Out of Scope: GCP Landing Zone setup (Folders, Projects, Organization-level IAM, Shared VPC) is assumed to be pre-configured by the Customer.
Physical decommissioning or hardware disposal of legacy Hadoop clusters.
Upgrading or patching legacy Hadoop source software versions.
End-user training or broad organizational data literacy programs.
Data cleansing or remediation of pre-existing data quality issues in the source Hadoop system.
Migration of any workloads, tables, or scripts exceeding the specific volumetrics (200 pipelines, 50 scripts, 750 SA tables) defined in this SOW.
Development of new Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards, PowerBI/Looker reports, or ML models not explicitly listed.
Historical Data Migration beyond the technical configuration of Connexio (Execution of the actual data transfer remains Customer's responsibility).
Third-party license fees for GCP, Connexio, or other software unless explicitly bundled.
Redesigning downstream application logic to consume BigQuery, except for providing the connection endpoint/credentials.
